subject: Pilot capacity alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Walker <evelyn.walker@novalia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot capacity alignment and next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Evelyn — good to meet the Novalia team. I wanted to capture what we discussed and propose concrete next steps so we can lock the pilot window and GPU reservations.

High-level recap
- Scope: 2-week evaluation of Redwood hosted inference for Novalia search personalization (text gen + embeddings).
- Success criteria (mutually agreed):
  - 99th perc p95 latency under 350ms for <1k tokens gen path during baseline load.
  - Embedding throughput >= 4k/sec with average latency <50ms for batched requests.
  - Cost per active session below $0.08/token-equivalent (as measured by our billing sim).
  - No PII exfiltration; keys remain scoped to Novalia project.
- Owners: Redwood (Priyom) will handle infra/provisioning and runbook; Novalia (Evelyn + IT) will provide sample traffic and evaluation prompts.

Capacity ask and proposed reservation
- Baseline reserved capacity: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved for the 2-week window).
- Autoscaling: enable 2x burst pool (on-demand) for short spikes up to 8 GPUs total; target warm-up for burst instances is 90s.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix cache for embeddings route to reduce token load by ~18%.

Attachments
- Attached a short MOP (redwood_pilot_mop.pdf) and a capacity estimate workbook (capacity_estimate_novalia.xlsx). The workbook has the traffic curves we discussed and cost projections for reserved + burst options.

Proposed timeline
1) Sign scope & SOW (DocuSign link) — target this week (EOD Thu 12 Aug).
2) Provision reserved capacity & test infra — Wed 11 Aug (Redwood infra lead).
3) Ground-truth traffic run and baseline eval — Thu 12 Aug.
4) 2-week evaluation window — 13–26 Aug.

Concrete next steps for Novalia
- Evelyn: share a redacted sample traffic dump and the top-50 evaluation prompts by Tue 10 Aug.
- IT: approve the outbound IP allowlist that we'll provide; we'll send the list today.

I'll move the SOW to DocuSign now and ping Marissa to coordinate provisioning when we have signed scope. If anything above looks off, flag it and I'll update.

Best,

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Evelyn Walker <evelyn.walker@novalia.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novalia IT Team <it@novalia.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity alignment and next steps

Thanks, Priyom — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications:

- Baseline traffic: we'll extract a 48-hour sample from production (anonymized) and send it by EOD Tue.
- On burst: can you confirm expected latency degradation during burst scale-up? We need to understand user-facing risk if traffic spikes.
- Security: we'll need a short runbook that lists all network flows and key rotation schedule for audit.

We'll review the SOW today. If DocuSign comes through, we'll aim to sign by Wed morning.

Evelyn
VP Product, Novalia

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Walker <evelyn.walker@novalia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Novalia IT Team <it@novalia.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity alignment and next steps

Evelyn — quick answers inline and added an internal note at the bottom for ops coordination.

- Burst latency: expected client-observed tail will increase by ~60–120ms during scale-up window (we warm new instances and populate KV cache). With our warm pool strategy we can usually keep impact closer to +60ms after the first 30–60s. For absolutely latency-sensitive endpoints we can configure a sticky-routing policy to prefer warm instances.

- Security runbook: attached a short MOP (redwood_pilot_mop.pdf) that includes network flows, IP lists, and key rotation cadence. We can expand for your auditor if needed.

Internal (Marissa / Ben) — action items for provisioning:
- Marissa: schedule reserved pool (4x A100-80GB equiv) for 13 Aug 00:00 UTC — ensure region us-west-2.
- Ben: enable autoscale policy with burst cap to 8 GPUs and set warm-pool size to 1 across the pool. Set alerting for sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 5m.
- Please populate the Drive folder (link in related_links) with the provisioning ticket and final runbook.

Evelyn — once we receive the traffic dump we will run the baseline sim and return a short eval matrix within 24 hours.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Novalia IT Team <it@novalia.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity alignment and next steps

All set on the provisioning side — reservation created and ticket #INC-7724 opened. Summary:
- Reserved: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent in us-west-2 from 2027-08-13T00:00:00Z to 2027-08-27T00:00:00Z.
- Burst pool: enabled up to 4 additional GPUs (8 total) with warm-pool of 1 instance. Warm-up TTL set to 120s and autoscale cooldown 180s.
- Alerts: GPU util >70% for 5m => slack @redwood-enterprise-ops and pager to Ben (oncall).

I've dropped the provisioning ticket and the runbook into the Drive folder. Evelyn, you should have access; ping me if not. Ben and I will run a dry-run of the traffic import at 11:00 today — Priyom, can you confirm you'll be available for a quick sync?

Thanks — Marissa
